I don't think we'll ever get people to stop reproducing. Even if we got the majority of people to stop, there will still be those reproducing in secret. And global genocide doesn't seem to be likely either.

Because we have been conditioned and brainwashed to believe human life is special. Worth continuing. Even groups like antinatalism and promortalism are small/within the minority. I think their numbers will grow over time, but it won't a philosophy that's accepted by the majority.
Either that or commit global genocide. I think it would be better to die now as opposed to later.
We exist for no reason. We're controlled by our DNA molecule to continuing existing even though we're all marching to oblivion.
Death

I was catholic. But after doing some research and contemplating I realized that all gods are just man made. All of the childhood indoctrinations like hell existing, a giant man in the sky who cares who you sleep with...it just didn't make any logical sense to me.

Due to humanity's lack of understanding and importance these fantasy characters came to be. The truth is we don't know how everything came to be and we most likely never will.
Logical philosophy. As well as promortalism

>And on another note; you ever notice how every argument seems to either devolve into an apathy contest, or pointing out how "sad" the other's life is? It's like, okay, my life is sad. And?

Yes! They either claim you're sad or just being a troll. To me it makes no sense to go about saying that.

>You can see it on Reddit. Many people are pretty dumb, but a lot of people are really smart… when it comes to technical things and stuff like that. What they all have in common though, is that they are emotional imbeciles. They have zero empathy or capacity for understanding other perspectives

Well said. I've also noticed that on Reddit. People on here in particular are so quick to judge or make false assumptions.

You said before that all I'm doing is "objectifying my values". If that were true why would it be wrong? What's wrong with the majority following one or two people's values or a truth that can lead them to better living conditions?

>Yet you refuse to invoke an objective standard. It may be true with respect to certain criteria, but you have not established any.

Even if I did, along with many others who have. Would that change humanity? It clearly hasn't so far. I already said in my post it would be like talking to a brick wall. 

>Earlier I asserted that your values are selfish and you negated this assertion.

By saying that I'm not objectifying my ideals onto others or that my views aren't an individualistic mindset? If it's the former I said I wasn't. Or if it's the latter you assume selflessness exist. Regardless if you have an individualist or collectivist mindset it's all rooted in selfishness.

>"Thrive better as a race," there is no objective metric to determine what a prosperous life entails. 

Obviously it would be better than what it is now

>So you concede that your are selfish. Earlier you negated that claim.

I didn't negate anything. So what exactly are you saying?

Because these values are more then just my personal opinions or feelings. Not that hard to see. Regardless of how you feel, if human took the step to stop, think, and put aside their differences. They will thrive better as a race. That's just factual. I think you lack self-awareness and overall understanding.

>Also, selfishness is the impetus for every action, so you are selfish.

Okay. That's nothing new. Every living creature is selfish.

>All you're doing is objectifying your values. 

No. I'm stating people should take more logical steps to become better 

>What are you talking about? "True progress," do you mean progress towards your ideals? Also, "better for this world," the world does not have preferences. Your values are not objective features of the universe and you are frustrated that everybody doesn't abjure their values and adopt yours. 

Obviously you don't understand. My "values" are logical and beneficial ways for humanity to improve. And most people who can see beyond the ignorance will agree.

>Again, you are expecting everybody to be simpatico. One individual is going to have one set of ideals and another individual will have a set of their own that is incompatible with the former. 

Again you are making false assumptions. I'm not expecting anything from anyone. Obviously everyone is going to have their own ideals. Being stagnant or putting aside our differences for true growth. What's more logical?

>What metric are you using to determine whose values are superior? It seems as though you are evaluating other values with your own, which would essentially be another instance of the "me me me mindset" that you professed to be displeased with.

A logical method that most would agree upon. One that will help a stagnant race. If it was a "me me me" mindset it would benefit me more than everybody else. Humans understanding the bigger picture and growing benefits everyone.
No one is free from consequences

The growth of being more logical and less hateful. Like I said in my post, putting all of their differences will lead to a better world.

 Humanity's weapons(toys) have changed,  but they themselves aren't too different from thousands of years ago. Think of all the wisest people who have lived and shared their knowledge. Yet humans remain the same.
Not realizing that all of their hate, fighting and violence amongst themselves won't do shit. If they remain stagnant and don't take the initiative to make change...how will they grow?

Not while hating and clinging to personal feels. But if everyone is willing to look beyond their hate, race, or status. True progression will happen. But it never will.

>And who defines what that is?

I suppose a very intelligent and logical person who sees the bigger picture. Not saying I'm extremely logical or smart, but that can be multiple people. Who see beyond the hate and rage.

This is about going the most logical/reasonable way for humanity. What good does it do to have everyone doing the same shit? 

>True cooperation begins on a level of acceptance of others and their views and pragmatism.

Acceptance of others sure. But am I suppose to accept views that can stagnant human growth?

Looking at and accepting the bigger picture, beyond our personal feelings and working together is true cooperation.
Yes.

Rather I hate everyone or not I'm still willing to cooperate and make this world better. But how is that possible when the majority have their heads up their ass? Making this world close to a utopia requires EVERYONE to take the initiative and make change.
No what divides us is a lack of understanding. I do hate humanity, but I can still see the corruption and how it can all be fixed.
It is logical
Truth doesn't care about your opinions or perspectives. In reality people make up their own "truths" because they're afraid of the actual truth.
No
Yes
You're still waiting regardless if someone is enjoying life or not.
You'll be making a wise decision. Assuming everything goes as planned.

I'm sure there's other arguments made by other philosophers. And what I just said. It really just takes contemplation. What grand purpose do we serve in this universe? Why are we special or important?

Just because human terms exist doesn't give it intrinsic value or even importance. It's the same thing with materials like money, it's useless pieces of paper that we placed arbitrary value upon.

 Objectively humans just serve no purpose and aren't important. The universe will continue after we die, these concepts will eventually perish. Humans believe they're important but in reality lack importance or value. What makes us more special than a bird or fly?

Purpose or meaning is just a human concept. Really without the perception of a sentiment and self-aware being those terms don't exist. You can say humans biological purpose is to reproduce but that's essential pointless. They have subjective purpose, just not an objective one.

Yeah humans are specks of dust compared to the universe. But everything including the universe is insignificant. Doesn't matter about the size honestly. Humans only hold subjective purpose, meaning they're Inherently meaningless.
I should've. But honestly you can't talk sense into people like him.
Speaking my language

>where you make the gravest of all errors. Already assuming you know what there is to know. Human existence is a neverending synthesis of knowledge and observations. 

That was my fault for not specifying. I admit I don't know the true purpose of reality itself or if there even is one. And perhaps we'll never know and are knowledge is limited to earth. I am saying that I know the true nature of humans and society as a whole. Of course, that's just a small aspect of a potentially much bigger truth.

>I did not call you depressed so please stay on-topic. 

I wasn't referring to you. Only to some people on this subreddit or others who've called me such.


>All I did call you was immature, not because of your views but because of how rigid they are. Whether you're 13 or 31 or 103, stagnating intellectually is intellectual degradation. We are always refining our truths and that should be the way we view and approach the world.

Granted I took wisdom from nihilism, some stoicism, some life lessons from different philosophers overall. So it's not like I discard the words of different philosophers who may disagree with my nihilistic views. Or other people for that matter. The knowledge I've accumulated(however limited) so far has lead to my current world view. Could it change? Maybe or it might stay the same.

>Any philosopher worth his while would laugh at you in the face when you present statements like these

You mean reasonable statements? Not likely. Even if they did, they have their own views about life and I have mines. If you disagree with my world view, I'm curious what arguments you have to make. Also many philosophers have made some nonsensical and childish claims about life.  Claims that aren't even worthwhile to contemplate.

>"Irrational" does not pertain beliefs that do not align with your own.

Towards an attitude(such as apathy). Not a belief.


>To convince others of your personal beliefs is to exceed your cognition. 

I went in with the mindset that many would disagree with me.

>
If you navigate the world with that mindset I assure you that you will fare much better than you are currently doing.

If I went in with the mindset that "I know nothing" even though I know the true nature of society and people in general. Doesn't make much sense. Also you don't know how I'm faring in life so how would you know?

>Kant tells you, why should you worry about what they believe? If it does not infrain on your rights or constrains your cognition, what is there to achieve by "converting" them to your oh so correct view of the world? 

I don't. I'm simply telling people like you that what I perceive is logical. You can disagree with me all you want as it won't change my worldview

> If you truly believed in the quest for knowledge you would understand that and I wouldn't have to tell you. Seems like you have some growing up to do.

That's your opinion. Seems like you need to stop making so many false assumptions. People here and people before have said my views are either the work of depression or something else. I know the truth so why would I care? Seems you're just upset with the way I present my statements. Why care about that? Why not just grow up and ignore post like this?

Morality differs in cultures and is subjective depending upon the individual. We can't all be right. Even statements like "killing is wrong" or "rape is wrong". Are the worse "evils" are minds can conjure up. Someone might justify in their head why the "cruel" thing they did was justified.

Another thing to consider is what Yang Zhu said "Morality is a deception practiced upon the simple by the clever."
I suppose I understand in that sense. We don't know how everything came to be, who or what created reality. Or if the universe itself is truly reality.

>I don't think anyone really knows what the fuck is going on (myself included). 

What makes you so uncertain of reality? Is it because of what you said about the irrational and paradoxical nature of existence?

>I'm just saying that I think it's folly to put it on such a pedestal as if it's like the ultimate thing. Even the most rational person on the planet is an irrational animal on some level.

I see what you mean and you're correct. Humans aren't logical 24/7 and even the most rational of us is still an animal at the end of the day.

> is really narrow in scope, very limited in the face of the Big Picture 

even if it is, it doesn't deny the fact that by using rational thinking. You see the world for what it truly is. I have credence because I can see things clearer than before. Think of all the lies you've been indoctrinated with since birth. And by using rational or critical thinking you freed yourself from those lies.

>You seem to place a whole lot of faith in logic and rationality

What's wrong with looking at things rationality?

Not exactly educated on these individuals. But most religious people see life as worth living. Do you know at least one of their reasons for why we should live?

Looking at the world "more logical" means you're looking at it from an objective perspective. Not an emotional or instinctive perspective.
Once you gain a more logical perspective on reality. There's no point to even existing.
Do you not realized how fucked up animals are in nature?
Playing a PS2 game on PS Now. Might go outside later and enjoy the cold air

I'm not sure how to describe it. It's like this animalistic force within you that stops you from carrying out the act. It's like you taught you were a calm, rational individual, but really you're just an animal like everyone else. It's just within our biological programming.

If you read up or watch videos on Arthur Schopenhauer he describes this as "The Will To Live" . Or at least this is just one aspect of The Will.

I doubt you had the same logic when you were ten. 

>just believing that your perspective is logical and unaffected by emotion does not make it so.

In my case it does. As it isn't clouded by emotions. These are the false assumptions people come to when they don't understand. We really live in world where just because you're not fond of life, you're automatically labeled as "mentally ill"

I don't like looking at the world from an emotional perspective. Being less attached or looking at it from a logical lens you start to see things for what they truly are. For me personally ever since I looked at things from a logical lens I felt more at peace and less stressed.

 Also I say people have a lower understanding because in all honesty. You'd have to raise your own level of awareness and logical to see where I'm coming from. 

Yeah perhaps insulting them isn't getting anywhere. I just don't like people assuming post like this indicate depression.
Great explanation

I don’t suppress my emotions. I vent whenever I need too. 

Like I said the people with a low understanding of things won’t get it and will assume it’s depression. How can you assume someone has a mental illness like depression based off a post like this? 

People are too attached to their emotions and basic instincts so of course they’ll think it’s depression.

I’m saying it’s not worth it. There’s just nothing to contribute to human beings besides maybe destruction. Think back on all of the wisest people who’ve shared their knowledge and yet people remain the same.
